headline: 28,090 cases: Dengue infections surpass last year's figure for same period
summary: A sharp rise in cases during August has pushed the total above last year's numbers, putting pressure on a healthcare system already strained by a measles outbreak.
details: A total of 28,090 dengue patients were reported between January 1 and August 22 this year, surpassing the 27,955 cases recorded during the same period in 2025, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
The surge is driven by a sharp increase in August, where 12,780 cases were recorded in the first 21 days alone, accounting for 45 percent of the total cases this year.
In the last 24 hours, 702 new dengue patients were admitted to hospitals, though no deaths were reported during this specific period.
While the overall death toll of 77 is lower than last year's 110 for the same period, the rising caseload is straining the country's healthcare resources.
The health sector is currently facing a 'double burden' as hospitals continue to admit around 900 measles patients a day, alongside the increasing dengue cases.
Major public hospitals in Dhaka are heavily occupied by measles patients, including the DNCC Dedicated Covid-19 Hospital, which has operated as a measles hospital since March.
DGHS Director (Hospital) Nurul Islam stated that they are coordinating with city corporations and public hospital heads to arrange additional beds to cope with the potential rise in patients.
caption:
Dengue cases in Bangladesh have officially surpassed last year's numbers for the same period, with nearly 45% of this year's total infections occurring in August alone.

A total of 28,090 dengue patients were reported between January 1 and August 22 this year, surpassing the 27,955 cases recorded during the same period in 2025, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

The surge is driven by a sharp increase in August, where 12,780 cases were recorded in the first 21 days alone, accounting for 45 percent of the total cases this year.

In the last 24 hours, 702 new dengue patients were admitted to hospitals, though no deaths were reported during this specific period.

While the overall death toll of 77 is lower than last year's 110 for the same period, the rising caseload is straining the country's healthcare resources.

The health sector is currently facing a 'double burden' as hospitals continue to admit around 900 measles patients a day, alongside the increasing dengue cases.

Major public hospitals in Dhaka are heavily occupied by measles patients, including the DNCC Dedicated Covid-19 Hospital, which has operated as a measles hospital since March.

DGHS Director (Hospital) Nurul Islam stated that they are coordinating with city corporations and public hospital heads to arrange additional beds to cope with the potential rise in patients.

headline_marked: DMP [[withdraws OCs of Tejgaon and Paltan stations]] citing administrative reasons
headline: DMP withdraws OCs of Tejgaon and Paltan stations citing administrative reasons
summary: Police Inspectors Kashainyu Marma and Mohammad Mostafa Kamal Khan have been reassigned to the DMP headquarters and central reserve office.
details: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has withdrawn the Officer-in-Charge (OC) of two police stations, citing administrative reasons.
The affected officers are Kashainyu Marma, OC of Tejgaon Police Station, and Mohammad Mostafa Kamal Khan, OC of Paltan Model Police Station.
According to an order signed by DMP Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed, both officers have been attached to the DMP central reserve office, headquarters, and administration division.
The order of withdrawal and attachment became effective from August 22.
caption:
Two high-profile OCs in Dhaka have been withdrawn from their posts.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has withdrawn the Officer-in-Charge (OC) of two police stations, citing administrative reasons.

The affected officers are Kashainyu Marma, OC of Tejgaon Police Station, and Mohammad Mostafa Kamal Khan, OC of Paltan Model Police Station.

According to an order signed by DMP Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed, both officers have been attached to the DMP central reserve office, headquarters, and administration division.

The order of withdrawal and attachment became effective from August 22.

#Bangladesh #Dhaka #DMP #PoliceNews #Administration

Source: Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV
